question: Insulin therapy is only required in Type 2 diabetes when all oral antidiabetic agents have been tried and failed.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is false. While insulin intensification is often stepwise in T2DM, early insulin initiation is indicated for: very high HbA1c at diagnosis (>10-11%), acute illness, symptomatic hyperglycaemia with catabolism, surgery, and pregnancy. It is not a last resort.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. Insulin may be required early in T2DM in several situations: acute illness/DKA-like presentation, pregnancy, pre-operatively, HbA1c >10-11% at diagnosis, or significant symptomatic hyperglycaemia. Insulin is not reserved only for oral agent failure.
